newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.S. sees no room for compromise on NATO post.
newsitem.headline: U.S. sees no room for compromise on NATO post.

text.p: The United States sees no room for compromise on French proposals that NATO's Southern Command be entrusted to a European officer instead of an American, a State Department spokesman said on Tuesday.
But U.S. officials suggested Washington was open to a greater role for Europeans in less senior positions.
The officials were speaking as U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher arrived in Paris for talks with French officials and an international meeting on Bosnia.
France, which pulled out of NATO's integrated command structure in the 1960s, is proposing to rejoin but wants a stronger role for Europeans in the structure.
It has suggested that the Naples-based post of commander of the alliance's southern region, currently held by U.S. Admiral Joseph Lopez, no longer be reserved for an American.

But State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns noted that NATO's chief asset in the region was the U.S. Sixth Fleet. "We want our Sixth Fleet under command of an American. It's a very important issue for us. I don't see any room for compromise.
"The American Congress is not going to support (the French proposal). The American people is not going to support it. And it's a bad decision," Burns told reporters.
But a senior U.S. official, speaking anonymously, said the United States was open to a greater role for Europeans lower down the command structure.
The official did not specify which posts might go to Europeans. NATO's Supreme Commander in Europe is also by tradition an American, currently General George Joulwan.
In recent years, the United States has increasingly accepted the idea of a stronger European role in the 16-nation alliance, dubbed the European Defence Identity.

U.S. officials expected NATO issues to come up at a working dinner Wednesday evening between Christopher and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette. They said however that apart from Bosnia the top issue was likely to be the eastern Zaire crisis.
